question: Where can I find, in consolidated form, the current legal texts that set the permitting procedure for energy projects in the United States, by technology and size?

answer.summary: Federal law is consolidated officially: eCFR (regulations, current to 2026-11-24, versions since 2017, API) and the U.S. Code (statutes through Public Law 119-142, XML). They hold e.g. FERC hydro licensing and exemptions for eligible projects up to 10 MW, QF 80 MW limit, offshore renewables, BLM rights-of-way and NEPA deadlines; CEQ's NEPA rules were removed in 2025. State authorization is in each state's code (e.g. MN 216I, NY PSL Art. 8 at 25 MW); local zoning is only compiled non-officially (NLR wind ordinances). Interconnection rules sit in FERC tariffs.
main_caveats: Permitting is split by level: federal review applies only with a federal nexus (federal land, funding, licence); states and localities authorize most onshore wind and solar.
CEQ NEPA regulations (40 CFR 1500-1508) were removed effective 2025-04-11; older guidance citing them is outdated.
Generator interconnection procedures are in each transmission provider's FERC tariff, not in the CFR.
Local zoning rules have no official national consolidation; the NLR compilation is AI-assisted and non-official.
answer.confidence_reason: Federal sources tested via API and downloads; state law sampled in 4 of 50 states (California blocked) and local rules only through a non-official compilation.

steps: Get current dates from titles.json, then use that date in structure/{date}/title-{n}.json to list parts.
Retrieve text with full/{date}/title-{n}.xml?part=...&section=... and send Accept-Encoding (curl --compressed).
Use versions/title-{n}.json?part=... for the dates when each section changed or was removed.

Energy procedures sampled: 18 CFR Part 4 (hydro licenses; Subpart K exemption of small hydro of 10 MW or less), Part 5 (integrated licensing), Part 50 (interstate transmission siting permits), Part 157 (gas certificates), Part 292 (PURPA qualifying facilities, 80 MW); 10 CFR Parts 50 and 52 (nuclear licensing, structure only); 30 CFR Part 585 (OCS renewable energy); 43 CFR Part 2800 (FLPMA rights-of-way, subpart 2809 solar and wind); 10 CFR Part 1021 (DOE NEPA procedures).
reading_traps: The full-text endpoint returns HTTP 406 'This endpoint requires response compression' unless Accept-Encoding allows compression.
40 CFR Parts 1500-1508 (CEQ NEPA regulations) are [Reserved]: sections were marked removed on 2025-04-11; agency procedures (e.g. 10 CFR 1021) and the statute now carry NEPA procedure.
Generator interconnection procedures are not in the CFR text: 18 CFR 35.28(f) only requires each OATT to include the standard procedures, so the operative text is in each tariff.
Thresholds differ by purpose: 18 CFR 4.30 defines a minor water power project as 1.5 MW or less, small hydro exemptions 10 MW or less, conduit exemptions up to 40 MW.

problems: www.ecfr.gov web pages redirect non-browser clients to unblock.federalregister.gov ('Request Access'); the /api/ endpoints answer normally.
